title: Buffett on buying businesses, not stocks: the 2020 CNBC Omaha interview on markets, rates, and Berkshire
summary: In his annual post-letter CNBC interview, Buffett argues stocks are businesses to own for decades, so daily selloffs and virus headlines should not change decisions. He covers interest rates, reaching for yield, bad incentives (Wells Fargo), and why Berkshire's conglomerate structure works.

principles.text: Think of stocks as businesses you will own for decades, not tickers to trade on headlines.
principles.quote: people would be better off if they say, "I bought a business today, not a stock today." Because that gives you a different perspective on it.

principles.text: Nobody can predict the market; the real question is whether you are paying a sensible price for future earning power.
principles.quote: if you get your money's worth in terms of future earning power over the next 10 or 20 or 30 years, you're going to have made a good investment.

principles.text: Write down why a business is worth its total market price, rather than guessing short-term price moves.
principles.quote: You should say, I am buying the General Motors Company for $42 billion because, and you should get it on a piece of paper.

principles.text: A market drop is good news for a net buyer who holds for the long term; it only hurts those forced to sell.
principles.quote: how can it be bad news unless you have to sell stocks? Now, if you have to sell them for some reason, it's you're worse off if you don't have to sell them.

principles.text: Reaching for yield is foolish; adapt your spending to your income, not your income to your spending.
principles.quote: You should always adapt your consumption to your income. You shouldn't try and adjust your income to your consumption.

principles.text: Incentive systems drive behavior, so a dumb one produces bad behavior, and problems must be attacked the moment they appear.
principles.quote: you can cause people to do the wrong thing because they will do what they're incented to do.
